author: OpenAI Codex assessment agent (current_assessments)
changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Rupert Lowe
metadata.description: British politician advocating substantially reduced immigration, lower taxes, deregulation and restoration of established national institutions and customs.
metadata.scope: Current documented governing or campaigning position through 4 October 2026. Recent conduct is prioritised; earlier material is used only as a stated continuity-based inference. Party proposals are attributed as the leader’s endorsed programme, not implemented law. Every answer is an interpretive assessment, with lower confidence for biomedical hypotheticals and fine-grained psychological causation. No scores were targeted.
metadata.role: Leader of Restore Britain and Member of Parliament

sources.title: Party launch statement by Rupert Lowe

axes.brief: His programme seeks electoral power, verified citizen voting and a binding death-penalty referendum; his parliamentary work scrutinises government administration.
axes.counterEvidence: Restricting postal voting and abolishing legal obstacles to deportation qualify the rights picture. Excluding people from his party is not the same as prohibiting opposition parties nationally.

answers.rationale: Inferred: regular electoral replacement provides the necessary mandate.
Inferred: expert advice should not replace an electoral mandate.
His electoral programme restricts voting by citizenship and verified eligibility, not education or intelligence. The citizen qualification in this question is therefore important.
Inferred: a rejected bill cannot acquire authority solely from the leader.
Inferred: equal contestation is part of legitimate electoral competition.
Inferred: public spending should face scrutiny beyond the governing leadership.

His reliance on statutory and jury protections supports independent remedies, but removing legal obstacles to deportation and restoring parliamentary control limits judicial supremacy. The balance concerns domestic constitutional review, not merely rejecting foreign courts.
Inferred: trade-union representation should not replace the general electorate.
Inferred: disagreement alone should not disqualify an electoral competitor.

The programme explicitly proposes a binding vote to restore capital punishment. This supports voters reversing an existing statutory settlement, while extending that mechanism to laws generally remains inferential.
Inferred: major decisions need institutions beyond the individual leader.
Inferred: serious abuse warrants a defined institutional removal mechanism.
Inferred: continuity alone cannot justify evading independently fixed election rules.

His emphasis on voter control and opposition scrutiny supports an additional electoral accountability mechanism. A general recall right is a modest extrapolation, not an expressly adopted recall scheme.
Inferred: even a strong executive must answer to voters or representatives.
Inferred: armed forces should not independently choose the government.

axes.brief: Civil-liberty and self-defence proposals coexist with strict enforcement of criminal and immigration law.
axes.counterEvidence: Free-speech commitments conflict with proposals to exclude anti-British teaching from publicly funded universities. Pepper spray is not equivalent to a firearm entitlement.

answers.rationale: Conditional inference: adult consent should outweigh paternalistic prohibition; balanced against the consideration that protective law can restrict dangerous choices even without immediate third-party harm.
Inferred: a serious-crime warrant supplies a proportionate security safeguard.
Inferred: public access and order can justify restricting disruptive assemblies.

Qualified inference. His liberty programme defends lawful criticism and whistleblowing, but his education proposals exclude supposedly anti-British teaching from public universities. The conflict weakens an unqualified free-expression response.
Inferred: self-regarding medical risk should normally remain voluntary.
Inferred: retention without individual suspicion exceeds proportionate policing.
Inferred: road safety justifies preventive checks without individual suspicion.
Inferred: a judicial finding of serious danger permits preventive restraint.
Inferred: adults retain access despite governmental moral disapproval.
Inferred: ordinary communication should not require government identity registration.
Inferred: a credible violence threat permits area-wide preventive searches.
Inferred: credible evidence of disorder can justify prevention.
Inferred: independent authorisation is needed absent an immediate emergency.
Inferred: public accountability can justify disclosure of official secrets.

His July criticism of handgun restrictions, combined with a broad self-defence programme, supports limited agreement. Pepper-spray legalisation alone would not establish firearm permission; the exact violence-check condition remains inferred.
Inferred: a security allegation cannot remove independent review indefinitely.

axes.brief: His programme seeks restoration of a common British social and cultural foundation rather than official multicultural accommodation.
axes.counterEvidence: Cultural conformity should not be converted into a claim that biological inheritance explains every behavioural difference.

answers.rationale: Inferred: common public expectations should prevail over competing migrant customs.
Inferred: shared services need not finance distinct customary arrangements.
Inferred: permanent membership entails learning and practising shared customs.
Inferred: separate inherited identity can conflict with full national integration.
Inferred: a common language should be the default institutional priority.
Conditional inference: national history should publicly acknowledge Indigenous communities; balanced against the consideration that ceremonies should stress undifferentiated national citizenship.
Inferred: public cultural funds should primarily preserve common inherited traditions.
Inferred: shared civic expectations should take precedence in conflicts.
Inferred: institutions can organise around one common calendar.
Inferred: national identity should rest chiefly on one predominant tradition.
Inferred: participation in common public life is preferable to isolated enclaves.
Inferred: public signage should reinforce a common language.
Inferred: families should cultivate national belonging above sectional identity.
Inferred: a generally applicable covering rule should not have this cultural exception.
Inferred: a common customary identity should be prioritised.
Inferred: public integration policy should teach common customs first.

axes.brief: His current programme seeks net reductions, deportation of irregular residents, removal of the asylum system and revocable conditions for noncitizens; a narrower spousal route and exceptionally skilled health workers remain.
axes.counterEvidence: The spousal and skills exceptions prevent equating the platform with no entry under any circumstances. A sponsor is not identical to state permission.

answers.rationale: Inferred: permanent intake should remain controllable within national capacity.
Inferred: national selection takes precedence over a general migration entitlement.

Skilled selection fits his exceptional-entry approach, but family routes and revocable residence mean skills are neither sufficient nor the only relevant criterion. The statement says normally, so qualified agreement fits.
Inferred: family claims remain subordinate to tighter intake or eligibility rules.
Inferred: permanent membership can remain selective despite a protection claim.
Inferred: irregular entry should normally result in removal.
Inferred: employer demand does not override national population policy.
Inferred: housing and services can outweigh aggregate economic gain.
Inferred: family admissions should not circumvent an overall limit.
Inferred: a job offer alone is insufficient without wider national selection.

Tight selection favours an accountable sponsor, while his framework also makes national contribution and directly assessed eligibility decisive. These competing selection principles do not support making employer or family sponsorship universal.
Inferred: a qualification alone should not create a residence pathway.
Inferred: the national intake limit can prevail even over a protection claim.
Inferred: ease of cultural integration can legitimately influence selection.
Inferred: welfare entitlement should be reserved chiefly to citizens.
Inferred: difference alone is not sufficient reason to expand intake.

axes.brief: National interest and security determine his willingness to use force; stronger domestic control does not require universal overseas intervention.
axes.counterEvidence: An emphasis on British priorities can limit commitments abroad while supporting deterrence; autonomous targeting is only a conditional inference.

answers.rationale: The foreign-policy programme permits deploying forces for national interests and advocates military leverage. This supports force beyond responding to an attack, but a precise offensive-war doctrine is not stated.
Inferred: avoiding combat normally outweighs faster coercive results.
Inferred: security warrants paying for a decisive capability advantage.
Inferred: credible imminent danger justifies anticipatory defence.
Conditional inference: defensive necessity should sharply limit military action; balanced against the consideration that serious interests may justify force before an attack occurs.
Inferred: a professional force and voluntary service are preferable.
Conditional inference: preventing war can justify a weaker bargaining position; balanced against the consideration that major concessions may invite greater future insecurity.

Conditional inference: supervised military systems may delegate individual engagements; balanced against the consideration that human responsibility should include meaningful control of lethal decisions.
Inferred: defence should avoid extensive foreign campaigns.
Inferred: an attacked ally can justify armed intervention.
Inferred: credible defence requires sustained operations abroad.
Inferred: an unsettled claim is preferable to starting a war.
Inferred: credible military leverage is a legitimate bargaining instrument.
Conditional inference: de-escalation should prevail over a symbolic show of resolve; balanced against the consideration that demonstrated resolve can be necessary despite escalation risk.
Inferred: intelligence advantages justify some diplomatic costs.
Conditional inference: reciprocal security can justify reducing military capacity; balanced against the consideration that capability should not be traded away on insufficient security assurances.

axes.brief: The platform reserves authority to British institutions and rejects externally imposed constraints on its domestic programme.
axes.counterEvidence: Voluntary trading and security cooperation remain possible without accepting a political federation or superior external court.

answers.rationale: Inferred: domestic institutions should retain ultimate lawmaking authority.
Inferred: national consent should not be displaced by external decisions.
Inferred: domestic constitutional authority should be final.
Conditional inference: durable alliances justify limits on unilateral action; balanced against the consideration that commitments should remain subordinate to freedom of national action.
Inferred: a sovereign state must retain an exit option.
Inferred: domestic officials should remain under final national jurisdiction.
Inferred: national obligations prevail over external institutional objectives.
Inferred: environmental cooperation should retain final domestic control.
Inferred: independent foreign policy should not be surrendered.
Inferred: external institutions should not dictate national rights law.
Inferred: currency decisions should remain nationally accountable.
Conditional inference: shared problems can justify common funds and decisions; balanced against the consideration that cooperation should avoid transferring substantive decision authority.
Inferred: entry decisions must remain finally national.
Conditional inference: reciprocal rules can justify restraints on unilateral trade policy; balanced against the consideration that national discretion should prevail over binding common trade rules.
Inferred: political union would transfer too much national authority.
Inferred: immediate national interest should determine enforcement participation.

axes.brief: His parliamentary economic argument favours a larger private sector and less state direction.
axes.counterEvidence: Restoring the NHS is an explicit objective; protecting access need not determine ownership of every facility.

answers.rationale: Inferred: ordinary commerce should generally remain in private hands.
Inferred: regulation can secure utility goals without public ownership.
Inferred: equal service outcomes favour private rather than state ownership.
Inferred: competitive markets should normally be left to private enterprises.

His general preference for a larger private sector points toward private provision, while his specific health programme retains the NHS as the organising institution. Together these support mixed provision rather than a general private-facility rule.
Conditional inference: rail networks are appropriate public infrastructure; balanced against the consideration that rail infrastructure can be privately owned under suitable rules.

His preference for reducing state burdens and competitive delivery supports contracting on the stated lower-cost, equal-access terms. This concerns the service provider, not necessarily selling public assets.
Inferred: banking should generally be privately provided and regulated.
Inferred: commercial assets should normally return to private ownership.
Conditional inference: public landlords are needed at a substantial scale; balanced against the consideration that housing should remain predominantly privately supplied.
Inferred: effective regulation makes nationalisation unnecessary.
Inferred: private operators and royalties can protect the public interest.
Inferred: competitive contracting is preferable to public operation.
Inferred: sale and regulation can meet strategic needs more efficiently.
Inferred: persistent subsidy dependence is a reason to privatise.
Inferred: broadcasting should not require a state-owned provider.

axes.brief: Rebuilding national industry and energy security qualifies his otherwise business-friendly and deregulatory economic position.
axes.counterEvidence: Domestic preference does not entail identical barriers in all consumer markets; strategic ownership restrictions are distinct from tariffs.

answers.rationale: Conditional inference: domestic capacity warrants border protection; balanced against the consideration that foreign competition should normally be admitted without protective duties.
Inferred: consumer and competitive gains outweigh protecting incumbent sales.
Inferred: national capacity justifies paying a procurement premium.
Inferred: businesses should generally choose the most favourable supplier.
Inferred: resilience warrants protecting essential domestic production.
Conditional inference: lower import costs can benefit the country without reciprocity; balanced against the consideration that barriers should be removed through reciprocal concessions.

Industrial capacity is a policy priority, but the concrete incentives are investment deductions rather than an infant-industry import ban. Industrial preference and his competitive-market approach pull in different directions on this specific restriction.
Conditional inference: investment should generally compete regardless of nationality; balanced against the consideration that domestic or strategic interests can justify different terms.
Inferred: domestic food capacity merits special protection.
Inferred: competitive adaptation is preferable to shielding businesses.
Inferred: reciprocity can justify tariffs against imposed barriers.
Inferred: tax rules should normally be neutral between foreign and domestic products.
Inferred: foreign subsidies can justify corrective trade measures.
Inferred: mutual market access can justify some increased dependence.
Inferred: strategic ownership requires screening beyond investment value.
Inferred: consumers should normally access foreign digital providers.

axes.brief: His committee remarks favour freeing businesses from state burdens rather than assigning production through government.
axes.counterEvidence: Infrastructure and energy-security projects are exceptions to laissez-faire, but not comprehensive national production schedules.

answers.rationale: Inferred: firms should usually choose output in response to demand.
Inferred: strategic encouragement need not become compulsory production quotas.
Inferred: supply and demand should normally determine prices.
Conditional inference: public strategy should direct capital to priority industries; balanced against the consideration that investment should generally follow decentralised commercial judgement.
Inferred: consumer demand should normally determine business scale.
Inferred: supply incentives and market signals argue against administrative prices.
Inferred: entrepreneurs should not need to prove a production shortage.
Inferred: bank credit should normally follow decentralised risk and return.

He favours fewer business restrictions; a remittance levy makes transfers costlier but is not government permission to transfer. Qualified agreement preserves that distinction while recognising the targeted restriction.
Conditional inference: development goals can justify selective public support; balanced against the consideration that investor and consumer choices should determine industrial growth.
Inferred: monetary innovation should be permitted alongside public money.
Conditional inference: a statutory wage floor protects workers’ bargaining position; balanced against the consideration that pay should be set without a statutory floor.
Inferred: ordinary wages should follow employer-worker bargaining.
Inferred: institutional autonomy protects monetary policy from production directives.
Inferred: rental supply and prices should generally respond to demand.
Inferred: normal production and distribution should remain decentralised.

axes.brief: Tax reduction and a smaller state receive priority over narrowing income differences through cash transfers.
axes.counterEvidence: A safety net and healthcare can coexist with low redistribution; defence of taxpayers need not mean abolishing every benefit.

answers.rationale: Inferred: income equalisation is not an overriding fiscal purpose.
Inferred: unequal earnings alone do not justify additional tax.
Inferred: tax burdens constrain expansion of cash entitlements.
Inferred: benefits should chiefly prevent hardship, not equalise lifestyles.

His fiscal case weighs retained earnings against financing a safety net. Low business taxes and opposition to inheritance taxation do not settle whether higher earners should pay substantially larger income-tax shares. The competing fiscal purposes support a conditional answer.
Inferred: retaining earnings should take priority over further equalisation.
Inferred: family transmission should not be taxed primarily for redistribution.

His work requirement removes benefits for refusal, while protecting vulnerable recipients. Conditional entitlement is not automatic expiry despite continuing poverty; support versus incentive concerns remain mixed on that additional rule.
Inferred: asset ownership should not be taxed chiefly to redistribute wealth.
Inferred: containing the taxpayer burden limits benefit generosity.
Conditional inference: adequacy extends beyond bare subsistence; balanced against the consideration that income benefits should focus on essential needs.
Inferred: retained income and incentives deserve fiscal priority.
Conditional inference: public supplements can support people in low-paid work; balanced against the consideration that wages should not routinely be supplemented through taxpayer transfers.

His flat-rate proposal concerns corporation tax. For workers, rewarding extra effort favours flatter rates while funding a safety net can retain progression; equal marginal income-tax rates are not established.
Inferred: property rights and market transfer should normally determine landholding.
Inferred: eligibility should focus on households unable to meet essentials.

axes.brief: Cultural restoration gives inherited Christian institutions a public place while civil national institutions retain legal authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposition to Islamist influence is not by itself a demand for Christian religious courts or clerical vetoes.

answers.rationale: Inferred: civil reasons should justify enforceable laws.
Inferred: religious conviction should not itself determine civil law.
Inferred: government must retain authority without clerical permission.
Inferred: the state may formally recognise inherited religious foundations.
Inferred: schools should teach understanding without requiring belief.

Inferred disagreement. His programme calls for stronger teaching of Christian heritage but expressly frames it as historical literacy rather than religious instruction. Public recognition therefore does not justify a claim that public schools should cultivate faith.
Inferred: courts should apply civil enactments rather than clerical rulings.

Conditional inference: religious offices should have formal consultative or reviewing authority; balanced against the consideration that religious advice should not receive an official legislative privilege.
Inferred: inherited public worship can remain part of official ceremony.
Conditional inference: religious life can be a public purpose deserving support; balanced against the consideration that public funds should not chiefly cultivate religious adherence.
Inferred: religious symbols can express legitimate inherited public culture.
Inferred: official recognition of inherited festivals should continue.
Conditional inference: public office should not follow automatically from religious rank; balanced against the consideration that established religious offices can warrant institutional seats.

He supports church preservation and Christian heritage, but those are cultural and charitable purposes. Privileges specifically for religious activity beyond ordinary charity exemptions pull against his broader insistence on common legal rules.
Inferred: civil marriage should not depend on religious consent.
Inferred: civil family law should retain exclusive binding authority.

axes.brief: He advocates restoring established family, education and national-cultural norms rather than prioritising new identity conventions.
axes.counterEvidence: Institutional restoration may involve rapid political reform; preference for old social norms does not require gradual government reform.

answers.rationale: Inferred: established customs deserve priority over rapid value shifts.
Inferred: continuity should guide social expectations.

Conditional inference: social recognition should not depend on the traditional household form; balanced against the consideration that society should retain a special preference for established family forms.
Inferred: complementary inherited roles merit social encouragement.
Conditional inference: marriage should be available without a sex-based restriction; balanced against the consideration that marriage should retain its traditional sex-specific definition.
Inferred: the established married-parent model deserves social encouragement.

Mixed inference. The social programme seeks to reverse abortion changes concerning late pregnancy. That is not the same as condemning every early abortion. His preference for family continuity points toward caution, while the stated late-pregnancy boundary limits how far the position can be extended.
Inferred: parents should be able to withhold conflicting school instruction.
Conditional inference: parental suitability need not depend on the couple’s sex; balanced against the consideration that traditional parental complementarity deserves preference.
Inferred: inherited modesty norms should continue shaping public conduct.
Inferred: shared inherited categories should not be displaced by personal identification.
Inferred: intergenerational continuity should take precedence.
Conditional inference: nontraditional roles should receive equal social respect; balanced against the consideration that society may prefer inherited sex-specific roles.
Inferred: durable institutions require measured change.
Inferred: school instruction should remain constrained by traditional family values.
Inferred: historical continuity can itself justify retaining a custom.

axes.brief: He supports automation, energy development and faster reservoir construction, while protecting countryside from housing development and challenging medical risk decisions.
axes.counterEvidence: Countryside protection contradicts a general development-first label. Biomedical and embryo judgments remain qualified analogies from bodily autonomy, safeguarding and inherited human continuity, not recorded technology-specific proposals.

answers.rationale: Inferred: early benefits can justify wider use before complete long-term knowledge.

His opposition to institutional risk-aversion supports wider adoption after proportionate checks. The question asks substantial risk evidence, not certainty; medical and irreversible harms remain exceptions in this assessment.

Accelerated reservoirs and energy projects favour construction, while the same programme protects countryside from housing development. The habitat trade-off is therefore conditional rather than blanket agreement.
Conditional inference: medical deployment needs evidence beyond immediate benefit; balanced against the consideration that basic demonstrated safety may justify access before long-term study.
Inferred: productivity and retraining can justify disruptive adoption.

Countryside preservation and opposition to extensive housing weigh toward restraint; reservoirs and energy-security projects weigh toward development. Neither receives a universal priority across the programme.
Inferred: food-system novelty warrants more evidence before substitution.
Inferred: elective invasive enhancement warrants strong long-term evidence.
Inferred: innovation can be preferable to restraining consumption.
Inferred: public need can justify proceeding with proportionate mitigation.
Conditional inference: adult consent can justify access despite residual uncertainty; balanced against the consideration that basic safety alone is inadequate for invasive elective enhancement.
Inferred: diagnostic reliability across patient groups is a prerequisite.
Inferred: heritable enhancement crosses an ethical or precautionary boundary.

Conditional inference: widespread cultivation needs a robust ecological evidence threshold; balanced against the consideration that managed early evidence can suffice without waiting for long-term certainty.

The programme explicitly resists building over countryside and seeks to reduce housing demand through immigration policy. Its support for essential infrastructure qualifies, but does not reverse, that land-preservation preference.
Inferred: potentially irreversible damage warrants a strong evidence threshold.

axes.brief: His proposal to repeal Scottish hate-crime legislation through Westminster favours final UK authority in constitutional disputes.
axes.counterEvidence: Local economic and property autonomy remain relevant; hostility to one devolved law does not establish central operation of all local services.

answers.rationale: Conditional inference: regional institutions need protected room to disagree; balanced against the consideration that national authority can override regional policy disagreement.
Inferred: a common state needs final national authority in disputes.
Inferred: the national union cannot be dissolved by a single regional vote.
Inferred: nationwide programmes can take precedence over regional refusal.
Conditional inference: regions can define their institutions within national rights; balanced against the consideration that constitutional organisation should remain centrally determined.
Inferred: policing should remain principally regional or local.
Inferred: local fiscal responsibility warrants keeping most local receipts.
Inferred: common knowledge and standards justify national content.
Inferred: local democratic priorities can justify different tax rates.
Inferred: workers should have common national employment guarantees.
Conditional inference: local voters should control their institutional arrangements; balanced against the consideration that changes to local public authority require national oversight.
Inferred: common entitlement warrants nationally defined coverage.
Inferred: a common citizenship framework should govern local authority.
Conditional inference: national coordination prevents harmful fiscal competition; balanced against the consideration that regions should remain free to attract activity through tax choices.
Inferred: contained local effects justify regional decisions.
Inferred: cross-regional emergencies justify coordinated national command.

axes.brief: His programme relies on education, incentives and cultural institutions to change conduct; this provides a social-learning inference.
axes.counterEvidence: His physical-sex claims are not a theory of behavioural heritability. Education, family continuity and individual differences support mixed trait-specific analogies; no empirical racial-causation claim is attributed without evidence.

answers.rationale: Inferred: social formation is the stronger general explanation.
Conditional inference: hereditary variation is treated as the stronger explanation; balanced against the consideration that education and conditions better explain cross-country scores.

His programme makes firm claims about physical sex while also relying on upbringing and institutions to shape conduct. Physical classification does not establish which cause explains most behavioural differences; the two commitments support a mixed inference.
Conditional inference: biological vulnerability is given more weight than experience; balanced against the consideration that experience and surroundings receive greater weight in stress response.
Inferred: opportunity and experience primarily cultivate interests.
Conditional inference: risk appetite is weighted toward inherited disposition; balanced against the consideration that learning and experience primarily shape risk tolerance.
Inferred: institutions and upbringing are the stronger source of cooperation.
Conditional inference: inherited variation is weighted above social formation; balanced against the consideration that relationships and social experience primarily shape empathy.
Conditional inference: experience and environment receive greater causal weight; balanced against the consideration that biological predisposition is weighted more heavily for attention.
Conditional inference: immediate moral reactions are attributed primarily to predisposition; balanced against the consideration that moral learning and culture are weighted more heavily.
Inferred: experience and social learning chiefly shape perceived threats.
Conditional inference: stable inherited dispositions receive greater explanatory weight; balanced against the consideration that social formation and experience receive greater explanatory weight.
Conditional inference: learned conventions and personal experience are weighted more heavily; balanced against the consideration that inherited preferences receive greater explanatory weight.
Inferred: social context and upbringing are favoured over racial heredity.
Inferred: self-control is teachable rather than principally racially inherited.

Conditional inference: occupational output or market valuation is weighted above social expectations; balanced against the consideration that social expectations and opportunity are weighted above intrinsic economic difference.

review.notes: Independently read all 240 exact questions, their rationales and directions, all briefs and counter-evidence. Reopened party programmes, the May parliamentary hearing, GB Politics interview and July LBC context; added substantive immigration, elections, liberties, industry and justice pages. Corrected flat corporation tax versus workers’ marginal rates, welfare work conditions versus automatic expiry, remittance taxation versus prior approval, sponsorship versus state selection, funding versus healthcare ownership, and industrial incentives versus import restrictions. The countryside policy reversed an unsupported blanket housing-development inference. Physical sex was separated from behavioural causation; firearm reasoning now uses his July comments rather than pepper spray alone. Moderated recall and offensive-force inferences and removed repetitive full-brief boilerplate. All conditional neutrals retain competing principles, with lower-confidence hypothetical biomedical and psychological extrapolations explicitly labelled. No scores were targeted; shared portrait and full-catalogue similarity checks are integration steps. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.
